applicabilityBasis.summary: USDp is marketed for payments and transfers with a one-dollar target, but users mint, burn and redeem through Parallelizer contracts against digital-asset collateral. Proportional redemptions can incur penalties and do not establish payment of national currency or a national-currency bank deposit by a legal issuer. The factsheet identifies a DAO-governed protocol as issuer and Cooper Labs as builder. Payment marketing alongside these protocol-level digital-asset exits creates documented ambiguity under GENIUS Act section 2(22).

genius.notes: Assessment concerns Parallel USDp, not Paxos USDP. Parallel V3 is the protocol attribution in the factsheet; Cooper Labs is the disclosed builder and keeper, not a verified legal payment-stablecoin obligor. issuerEntity and issuerDomicile are omitted. Public protocol collateral disclosure is present, but it is not an independent reserve attestation. The reviewed redemption mechanism returns backing digital assets and is not a fiat redemption promise. This follows the documented-ambiguity treatment used for LUSD, BOLD, GHO and USDS rather than treating all CDPs as categorical non-payment tokens.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: The bounded public-source review found no qualifying GENIUS approval, state qualification, official pending application or foreign registration naming Parallel USDp or a disclosed legal issuer of this token. Protocol development, collateral issuers and unrelated bank applicants were not treated as token-level authorization. The finding does not exclude confidential or unpublished submissions.
